html:
Mbandzeni was king of the Swazi from 1875 to 1889, during whose reign almost the whole country was signed away to European concession seekers.

After gold was found nearby in the 1880s, Boer and British prospectors, farmers and traders flocked to him. In return for cash and gifts he granted concessions over land, grazing, mining, customs, railways and even the right to collect taxes, often overlapping and covering the same ground.

The concessions led to the Transvaal taking control of Swaziland in 1894, and to British rule after the South African War. A partition in 1907 left the Swazi with only about a third of their land. Winning it back became the life work of Sobhuza II and the people of Swaziland, who had kept Mswati II's kingdom whole until then.
sum: Mbandzeni was king of the Swazi from 1875 to 1889, during whose reign almost the whole country was signed away to European concession seekers.
